title: Your AI Agent Has No Nervous System — Matt Gibiec, Dynatrace
talk_summary: A Dynatrace solutions engineer argues that AI agents fail mainly because they lack environmental context (dependency maps, production telemetry, change history), and pitches 'Blue Box', a product that injects that context into coding agents across the SDLC. It is almost entirely a product pitch with no measured results; the only transferable ideas are generic context-engineering and pre-planning practices.

takeaways.technique: Inject dependency/production context into agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Feed agents service dependency maps and production behavior data so changes are evaluated against what else the change touches, not just local tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we will be able to bring that essentially services and dependency mapping for every single one of your agents

takeaways.what_they_do: Overlay what changed (commits, merges) on observed anomalies to attribute issues to a specific change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we will now also have the context of what was changed in your ecosystem

takeaways.what_they_do: Do upfront research on what a feature must deliver and what existing agents/apps it interacts with before any code is written.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We'll be able to actually plan before you prompt.

takeaways.what_they_do: Structure automation as observe -> detect -> suggest fix -> human decides to ship, keeping a human gate at the end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: giving you the control at the end of it, to make the decision whether you want to push the feature out there
